answer.justification: Median first divergence is 1 and edit distance is 0.772, which is close to the system-prompted range (median 0, 0.79-0.82). It is far from quantized (10-17, 0.52-0.57) and from fine-tuned (5.5-8, 0.56-0.65). Exact match is 0.016, which is only slightly above the system-prompted 0.000 and is also seen in the other categories, so it does not separate them. Early divergence points to a hidden instruction changing the opening. Refusals added (9), disclaimers (23.4%) and very short replies (29.7%) all rose, which exceeds the fine-tuned range of 0-4 refusals added. A hidden prompt could plausibly cause this by making the model more cautious and terse. This is unusual for the documented system-prompted models, which added at most 1 refusal. A fine-tune with stronger effects is the main alternative. Logit and activation data are missing, so confidence is moderate.
